data.name: Supermarket Tycoon
data.detailed_description:
Please Note: This game is in Early Access meaning it's not fully complete and missing some content. Please be ready to expect bugs.
Supermarket Tycoon is a strategy and simulation game that lets you build up your own store from the bottom up. Go from rags to riches or from riches to rags. Sell what you want how you want! Catch thieves, build your store, stock shelves, and much more!

Gameplay Overview
Supermarket Tycoon allows you to build your own store from scratch. Design your store from scratch, decide what to sell, hire employees, catch thieves, take out loans, attract customers, profit.
Story Mode - Start from scratch and build up your store. Accumulate profit, expand your store, hire employees, take out loans, get rich, go broke.
Sandbox Mode - Use unlimited resources to build your own store

Key Features
- Design your store
- Full Sandbox
- Loans
- Hire Employees
- Expand your store

Developers twitter: @sneakthiefgame
Audio by: @young_zxnder

reviews.review:
Supermarket Tycoon is a retail management simulator developed and published by Nicholas Rizzo that invites players to build a thriving supermarket from a humble beginning. Centered on the familiar tycoon formula of earning profits, expanding facilities, and making smart business decisions, the game focuses on the satisfaction of watching a small grocery store evolve into a bustling shopping destination. While its presentation is relatively simple, the core concept captures the rewarding progression that has made business simulation games popular among fans of the genre.

The experience begins with limited capital, encouraging players to think carefully about every purchase and expansion. Shelving, checkout counters, refrigeration units, and other store fixtures must be positioned efficiently to create an inviting shopping environment while maximizing customer flow. As profits increase, additional departments and product categories become available, allowing the supermarket to grow beyond groceries into areas such as electronics, clothing, automotive products, beverages, and household goods. This steady expansion provides a constant sense of accomplishment as the store gradually transforms into a larger retail operation.

Managing inventory is only one part of the challenge. Running a successful supermarket also requires overseeing employees who handle various responsibilities throughout the business. Staff members such as managers, janitors, and security personnel each contribute to smoother daily operations, reducing the workload on the player while introducing new financial considerations. Hiring the right employees at the right time becomes an important strategic decision, particularly when balancing operating costs against growing revenue. The inclusion of security mechanics also adds realism, reminding players that protecting merchandise is just as important as selling it.

One of the game's strengths is its flexibility. Players looking for structured progression can enjoy Story Mode, where careful financial planning and gradual expansion are essential to success. Those who prefer unrestricted creativity can switch to Sandbox Mode, which removes many economic limitations and allows complete freedom to design the supermarket of their imagination. This combination gives the game broader appeal by accommodating both players who enjoy overcoming economic challenges and those who simply want to experiment with layouts and store designs.

Visually, Supermarket Tycoon favors functionality over graphical spectacle. The environments are clean and easy to navigate, ensuring that products, employees, and customer activity remain clear even as the store becomes increasingly busy. Although the graphics are modest by modern simulation standards, they effectively support the management-focused gameplay. The interface generally presents important information in an accessible way, though some aspects of the controls and menu navigation reflect the game's unfinished Early Access status and could have benefited from additional refinement.

The game's strongest moments come from its satisfying progression loop. Expanding the sales floor, unlocking new merchandise, increasing customer traffic, and steadily improving profits create a rewarding rhythm that keeps players invested for many hours. There is genuine enjoyment in watching a once-empty building develop into a lively commercial business through careful planning and strategic investment. Players who appreciate optimization and gradual economic growth will likely find this aspect particularly engaging.

Despite its promising foundation, the experience is held back by its incomplete development. Many planned features and deeper management systems were outlined during its Early Access period, but the final product never fully reaches the ambitious scope originally envisioned. Some mechanics remain fairly basic, long-term content becomes repetitive after extended play, and the simulation lacks the complexity found in more polished retail management games. As a result, the game can feel like a solid prototype rather than a fully realized business simulator.

Even with these shortcomings, Supermarket Tycoon succeeds in delivering an enjoyable retail management experience that captures the appeal of building a business from the ground up. Its accessible mechanics, satisfying progression, varied inventory, and flexible game modes make it an entertaining option for players who enjoy economic simulations, especially those willing to overlook its unfinished state. Although it falls short of becoming one of the genre's standout titles, it still offers enough engaging ideas to provide several enjoyable hours of strategic gameplay.

Rating: 5/10
